newsletter_description: Explore the powerful sculptural work of Melvin Edwards, a visionary artist whose art speaks to the African American experience.
description:
The Newark Museum of Art is deeply saddened by the loss of artist Melvin Edwards (1937-2026) who passed away on March 30. Edwards originally trained as a painter and was passionate about experimenting with various artistic mediums to invent new sculptural pieces that he felt were new to the world. He became internationally known for his welded steel sculptures depicting objects associated with violence against African Americans. His iconic Lynch Fragments series, started during the height of the civil rights movement, incorporate chains, nails, and padlocks, bridging abstract and narrative forms. Inspired in part by African masks, these wall-mounted sculptures call to mind faces looking, pointing, and warning.
